text.p: The pound was firmer against the mark and steady against the dollar on Monday, trading in narrow ranges after a shake-out last week.

The UK currency consolidated around 2.63 marks and $1.60 in quiet trading. Dealers said the focus this week was the monetary meeting on Wednesday between Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George.
"There is some caution ahead of the monetary meeting on Wednesday -- as usual -- so sterling will consolidate for the time being," said a senior trader at a German bank in London.
Receding interest rate rise expectations and concern that the strength of the pound might hurt UK economic growth contributed to the sterling sell-off last week.

Sterling/yen, which also dropped sharply last week, firmed back above the 195 yen level, trading at 195.22/45 at 1100 GMT, up from 194.50 at the European close on Friday. Sterling/Swiss franc, meanwhile, was little changed at 2.2816/47.

The UK purchasing managers index was higher than expected, with price data showing the largest monthly drop since last August. The overall index rose to 54.0 in January, from 52.8 in December, well above above the 52.2 forecast.
The recovery in the overall index suggested manufacturing output might not be that badly hit by sterling strength, analysts said.

"Overall I think this is a strong survey that will allay fears that the manufacturing sector is going to stagnate due to the rise in the currency," said Ciaran Barr, economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell here.
The prices index dropped to 41.6 from 42.3, underlining the positive impact of a strong pound on input prices.
The PMI will add weight to BOE Governor George's calls for tigher credit but rates are expected to stay steady this week.
